In a settings Drawer, give peer sections consistent heading size, body inset and spacing. Align repeated labels and controls on shared tracks, then test with a narrow viewport and dense content so the footer stays reachable.

Uses Flood native Dialog focus containment, scroll lock, background inertness, nested layers and return focus. Escape and the named close IconButton dismiss it; closeOnOutsideClick defaults to true. Controlled open/onOpenChange and initialFocusRef match Dialog.
Drawer inherits getFallbackFocus from Dialog. Use it when saving or deleting can remove the opening row from a collection.

side is logical start/end or physical top/bottom. size sets 20/26/34rem for sm/md/lg, capped to the viewport. Vertical drawers occupy the viewport height; horizontal drawers occupy its width. Entry motion respects reduced motion; closing is immediate.

Choose width against a populated record. For longer messages and several controls, compare md and lg. Use the description slot for short context and compose independent body groups with Section or Fieldset. Keep persistent actions in footer.

The body scrolls with Flood ScrollArea while the header and optional footer remain visible when space allows. Responsive padding and full-width narrow descriptions preserve the reading area at enlarged text; if the chrome cannot fit, the whole panel can scroll rather than clipping the body. Footer actions are host-owned, without implicit save or close. No swipe/drag gesture or nested navigation engine is included. Available in 0.2.5.

name: Sheet
description: A bottom-aligned modal for short tasks, navigation and touch-friendly choices.
code:
<Sheet title="Project settings" trigger={props => <Button {...props}>Open settings</Button>}>
  <Field label="Project name">{control => <Input {...control} defaultValue="Flood" />}</Field>
</Sheet>
notes: When switching the same short task between Drawer and Sheet, share the draft, wording and actions. Keep the state in the host and verify both dismissal and focus restoration at each supported width.
Sheet shares Drawer's modal semantics, dismissal, focus restoration, scrollable body and optional footer. Its scrollbar fits in the panel padding. Placement is always bottom.
The panel grows with content up to its size limit. Keep actions that must remain visible in the footer and use ListBox for selectable options.
Use a sheet for touch navigation or short choices that benefit from a wider target. Anchored popovers and selects remain useful on desktop. Available in 0.2.12.

name: CopyButton
description: A clipboard action with stable geometry and localized result feedback.
code: <CopyButton value="npm install @flood-md/react" />
notes: Copies only on a user click. Requires a secure context and Clipboard API; onCopyError receives unavailable/denied errors. The host owns any manual-copy fallback. Native button ref and disabled semantics are preserved.

Localize copyLabel/copiedLabel/errorLabel. resetDelay restores the idle state after success. Labels reserve their common width and a live status announces the result. No remote data transfer is built in. Available in 0.2.5.
Use iconOnly for a square IconButton when the nearby content makes the copy target clear. The button keeps its accessible name and success or failure feedback.

name: ToastRegion
description: A host-controlled notification queue with timed, pausable messages and actions.
code: <ToastRegion items={[{id:"saved",title:"Changes saved",status:"success",duration:0}]} onDismiss={id => { /* Remove the item from host state. */ }} />
notes: The host owns items and removes them onDismiss. IDs must be unique/nonempty. limit controls visible items; queued timers start only when visible. Ordinary messages default to five seconds; error/action messages persist unless duration is explicit. duration=0 persists.

Timers pause on hover, focus and hidden documents. F8 focuses the first visible region without interrupting initial task focus; hotkey=false disables it. Use a single main region per document. Localize label/closeLabel and message/action text. Error messages announce as alerts; others use polite status.
The stack uses an overlay scrollbar when displayed messages exceed its height. Focusing a dismissal or recovery action reveals it within the stack.

placement is logical start/end. inline embeds the region in a host container; fixed mode uses ordinary document stacking, so place a contextual region inside a modal if needed. Action callbacks do not dismiss automatically. No global notification store or promise API. Available in 0.2.5.

name: AvatarGroup
description: A compact collection of avatars with a count or an optional list of additional people.
code: <AvatarGroup label="Project collaborators" items={[{id:"alex",name:"Alex Morgan"},{id:"sam",name:"Sam Lee"},{id:"june",name:"June Park"}]} max={2} />
notes: The native list composes Flood Avatar. IDs and names must be nonempty and unique IDs remain stable. max is a positive integer; the default shows four people.
The default overflow is a static count. Use overflowPresentation="popover" when readers need the remaining names. Translate overflowLabel and overflowTitle as needed.
Visible avatars retain their accessible names. The popover shows only the additional people and uses ScrollArea when the list grows. The button has clearance from the overlapping avatar row.
Supply presence on individual items when known. Visible avatars separate to give each presence mark clearance. Additional names in the popover retain their presence.
Use spacing="separated" to give each face its own space even without presence. The default auto layout overlaps avatars unless a visible presence mark needs clearance.

Use layout="fit" in a bounded toolbar, table cell or summary where the group should use one line. It shows as many faces as fit up to max, and the same overflow disclosure accounts for hidden faces. The default wrap layout shows up to max faces across lines.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: AuthorMeta
description: An avatar, a person’s name and optional secondary information on one shared axis.
code: <AuthorMeta name="Maya Chen" metadata={<Timestamp dateTime="2026-11-14">14 Nov</Timestamp>} />
notes: Use AuthorMeta for attribution in comments, activity entries and compact contributor rows. Use Avatar alone for an image-only person reference.
The avatar is decorative because the adjacent name identifies the person. Supply Timestamp for a date or concise text for a role. Optional presence adds an availability mark and its accessible label.
Use metadataPlacement="inline" for a short timestamp beside the name. Metadata can wrap onto the next line as space runs out. The default stacks metadata below the name.

Use nameOverflow="truncate" in a constrained row when the visible prefix still identifies the person. The full name is available on hover and keyboard focus when clipped. Choose one size for peer rows and keep lifecycle states and row actions in their own slots.

name: Comment
description: An attributed message with an avatar, optional timestamp and message actions.
code: <Comment author={{name:"Maya Chen", metadata:<Timestamp dateTime="2026-11-14">14 Nov</Timestamp>}}>The export is ready for review.</Comment>
notes: Use Comment for an attributed message in a review or conversation. AuthorMeta owns the avatar, name and date. The body and actions share the author text axis.

Pass the message as children. Use named ghost IconButton or icon-only CopyButton for secondary message actions. They appear on hover or focus without shifting the message and stay visible on touch. Use actionVisibility=always when an action must be discoverable at rest.

Pass onReply to show the standard reply action, and replyLabel to localize it. The host chooses where to open and focus the editor, and restores focus when cancelling. CommentThread items support the same callback.
Use CommentThread for related messages and Timeline in activity mode for chronological system events. Keep permissions, reply state and data in the host.
Use attachments for FileList and reactions for ReactionButton. Reactions share the command row, remain visible when secondary actions are quiet, and belong to this message.
Pass a ReactionPicker to reactionPicker. Its trigger stays visible next to existing reactions. An empty comment reveals it with the secondary actions.

name: CommentThread
description: A chronological list of related comments with shared spacing and optional dividers.
code: <CommentThread aria-label="Review comments" items={[{id:"one",author:{name:"Maya Chen"},body:"Please include the original attachment."},{id:"two",author:{name:"Sam Rivera"},body:"I found the source file."}]} />
notes: Provide stable unique IDs and items in the order readers should see them. Give the list a name using aria-label or a visible heading referenced by aria-labelledby.
Each item uses Comment for the author, message and independent actions. Pass nested replies under their parent. Depth stays semantic while visual indentation is capped to preserve narrow text widths.

Spacing separates top-level messages by default. Use dividers only when peers are hard to distinguish, and repliesDisclosure for long branches. Pair with CommentComposer for drafting. The host owns reply targeting, permissions and loading.

name: CommentComposer
description: A compact comment editor with optional reply context and a cancel command.
code: <CommentComposer label="Reply" placeholder="Write a reply…" sendLabel="Post reply" replyContext="Replying to Maya Chen" value="" onValueChange={() => {}} onSend={() => {}} />
notes: Use next to a CommentThread for a comment or reply. Supply localized context only when the reply target should be explicit.

The reply context sits above the input surface in a compact header and describes the editor for assistive technology. The input surface is shared with MessageComposer. The send action defaults to Reply with context and Post otherwise. Localize it with sendLabel. Enter submits and Shift+Enter inserts a line break.
If replies accept files in a narrow panel, set maxVisibleAttachments to keep the draft close to the visible file tags.
When cancellation removes the editor, the host should return focus to the initiating action. Preserve the draft on submission failure.

name: ReactionButton
description: A compact reaction toggle with a count and host-controlled selection.
code: <ReactionButton label="Helpful" icon="👍" count={6} pressed={false} />
notes: The label names the reaction, pressed identifies the current user's choice and count is the aggregate number of reactions.
Update pressed and count together after a host decision. The accessible name starts with the reaction label and includes the visible count.
Use reactions in Comment to keep them visible beside secondary commands. The ghost variant suits a mixed row of small icon actions.

name: ReactionPicker
description: An anchored chooser for adding a reaction from a small set of options.
code: <ReactionPicker options={[{id:"helpful",label:"Helpful",icon:"👍"},{id:"celebrate",label:"Celebrate",icon:"🙌"}]} onSelect={id => console.log(id)} />
notes: Supply a small set of distinct, named options. Icons are decorative. Each option needs an accessible label that names the reaction.
The chooser closes after selection and returns focus to its trigger. Arrow keys move through the option toolbar. Escape dismisses it.
Pass selected on options already applied by the current user. They remain interactive and use the same accent as a pressed ReactionButton. onSelect receives the ID and requested next selection state.
Use Comment reactionPicker next to its ReactionButton elements. The host controls reaction data, counts and which options are already applied.

name: StatusIndicator
description: A named state with a decorative dot, tinted chip or compact icon.
code: <StatusIndicator tone="success" label="All systems operational" />
notes: Place the lifecycle state beside the record name or in its own named field or column. Keep it separate from record actions. Use the same presentation and size for peer statuses.

The label stays on one line and reveals its full text on hover or focus if clipped. Choose a short, meaningful state name for dense rows. Use presentation="icon" with a recognizable state glyph and keep the full label for the tooltip and assistive technology.
Use presentation="wrap" for a prose-like message that should grow with its content. The dot is decorative. Use announce to opt into a polite live region for changing messages.

Use presentation="chip" when lifecycle states need a consistent tinted silhouette, such as in a status column or a record header. Choose the same size as peer Badge metadata. Long labels retain single-line truncation and the full-label tooltip.
Static labels do not announce by default. Tone is independent of wording and size. Use Badge for categorical labels and Alert for a message requiring more explanation.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: Figure
description: A native figure that keeps media and its caption together.
notes: Composes native figure and figcaption. The host supplies the image, chart, code or other self-contained content, including its own alt text or accessible name.
captionPosition controls DOM reading order as well as placement. Caption content may contain links. Native hidden, dir, lang, style and ref target the figure.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: Blockquote
description: A quoted passage with an optional compact attribution.
code: Good interfaces make room for what matters.
notes: Uses native blockquote; cite remains a source URL, while attribution is visible host-authored credit. Rich quote content and attribution are supported.
The logical leading rule follows RTL. Supply quotation punctuation as part of your actual content; the component does not invent a quotation or source.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: RevealValue
description: A masked read-only value with explicit reveal and optional copy actions.
code: <RevealValue value="flood_demo_3f089bf2" showLabel="Show token" hideLabel="Hide token" hiddenValueLabel="Token hidden" copyLabel="Copy token" copyable />
notes: Use for read-only tokens or identifiers that should start visually concealed. The mask has a fixed length and the value enters the rendered text only after reveal.
Name the show, hide and optional copy actions for their value. Enable copyable only when copying is a supported operation. Copy becomes available when revealed and writes the exact value.
Use visible and onVisibleChange when the host controls disclosure. Keep authorization and secret retrieval in the host. Use PasswordInput for editable passwords.

name: CopyableValue
description: A visible value with a compact copy action.
code: <CopyableValue value="https://flood.md/mcp" copyLabel="Copy server URL" />
notes: Use for a visible URL, exact identifier or short value that people need to copy. Name the action for that value and localize copiedLabel and errorLabel when needed.

Long values wrap by default. Set overflow="truncate" when a recognizable prefix is enough in a dense row. Only clipped values get a tooltip and keyboard stop. The copy action writes the full value in either mode.
Choose the code appearance for identifiers and short code values. Use CodeSnippet for commands that need a larger reading surface.

name: InlineCode
description: A small monospace code fragment that participates in running text.
code: <Text as="p">Import <InlineCode>@/ui/button</InlineCode> in your project.</Text>
notes: Native code semantics, bundled monospace stack and a quiet inline surface. Content is text; no HTML parsing or syntax highlighting is performed.
wrap defaults to true for long identifiers. wrap=false preserves the fragment on one line and the host must manage overflow. Use CodeSnippet for blocks of code and Kbd for keyboard input.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: Metric
description: A labeled value with optional contextual trend and supporting text.
code: <Metric label="Monthly revenue" value="$24,580" trend={{direction:"up",label:"12.8% higher",tone:"success"}} hint="Compared with the previous month." />
notes: Native definition-list semantics associate the label with its value, trend and hint. Values may be rich content; the host owns currency, number and locale formatting.

Keep the metric name short and recognizable at a glance. The label takes one line and reveals its full text on hover or keyboard focus when clipped. Use the unit, trend context or hint for supporting detail.
Pass unit for a quieter trailing unit on the same baseline, such as ms or GB. Keep prefixes and placement-sensitive symbols in the formatted value.

Use state=loading for a pending value and state=unavailable for a missing value. Pass value={null} when the application has no accepted value. The label stays visible and a localized loadingLabel or unavailableLabel is available to assistive technology.
Pass trend.context for the baseline or comparison period that belongs beside the change. It keeps the supporting text neutral even when the change has a semantic tone.

Trend direction and semantic tone are independent: a decreasing failure rate can be good. Its label must communicate the change without relying on the decorative arrow or color. No automatic percentage calculation is performed.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: MetricDelta
description: A compact directional comparison with an optional period or baseline.
code: <MetricDelta label="8% lower" direction="down" tone="success" context="vs last week" variant="chip" />
notes: Use for a change displayed on its own in a row or table cell. Inside Metric, MetricCard and MetricGroup use the trend object, which renders the same comparison.
Pass a localized label that says what changed. Direction describes the movement; tone describes its meaning for this measure. A drop in errors can be success.
Use plain when the value above already owns the emphasis. Use chip when the change needs a tint to stand out among adjacent values. Keep the period outside the tint.

name: MetricCard
description: A compact surface for a labeled measure, its comparison and optional history.
code: <MetricCard metric={{label:"Monthly revenue", value:"$24,580", trend:{direction:"up", label:"12.8% higher", context:"vs last month", tone:"success"}}} chart={<Sparkline label="Revenue dipped twice before reaching a six-month high" values={[19940, 22650, 21180, 23140, 21800, 24580]} />} />
notes: Use for a prominent metric in an overview or dashboard. Metric owns the label, value, unit and comparison. The card uses the existing Surface padding and elevation.

The label stays visible while the value, comparison and supplied chart render skeletons. Leave chartLoading unset for a shared request. Use chartLoading=true for pending history, including before a chart node exists, or false to keep valid history visible during an independent value request. An unavailable current value can still show available history.
The default md value is the focal point. Use size sm in dense grids. The comparison period stays secondary and the chart reads after the value.
The inline layout moves the sparkline below the metric as available width decreases. Use stacked for a wide plot below the value. Omit the chart when there is no meaningful historical series.
Use a named Sparkline for the same measure. The displayed value, trend baseline and chart interval should agree with the data.

name: MetricGroup
description: Related measures with aligned values and an optional shared surface.
code: <MetricGroup label="API performance" appearance="panel" items={[{id:"requests",label:"Requests",value:"1.2M"},{id:"latency",label:"Response time",value:186,unit:"ms"},{id:"availability",label:"Availability",value:"99.98%"}]} />
notes: Use for related measures users read together. The items use Metric for labels, values, units and comparisons. Labels stay on one line. Use a short name with a recognizable start, and put the scope or period in supporting content. Clipped labels reveal the full name on hover and keyboard focus.

Use layout=rows in a drawer, sidebar or summary column. Labels share the start edge and values share the end edge. In very narrow containers, each value moves under its own label. Choose the layout independently of appearance.
Each item can independently be ready, loading or unavailable. Keep real zero values visible and localize state labels when needed.
Use plain inside an existing section and panel for a shared standalone surface. Set minItemWidth when the localized values or units need more room. Tracks reflow based on available space.
Choose MetricCard for a measure that needs its own chart and surface. Supply stable item IDs and the group's accessible name.

name: Sparkline
description: A compact line or area chart for trends in a table cell, list or metric.
code: <Sparkline label="Revenue rose from $8,000 to $12,000" values={[8000, 8200, null, 9500, 11000, 12000]} domain={[0, 15000]} />
notes: Give the graphic a label that communicates the metric and the trend. Set showLabel to make that label visible.
Use a shared domain for comparing magnitudes across rows. Null and nonfinite samples leave gaps in both the stroke and area.
The default area uses an accent stroke with a gradient below it. Choose variant line for stroke only and use semantic tones only when the data has a known interpretation.

name: LineChart
description: A line or area chart for comparing trends on a shared scale.
code:
<LineChart label="Daily visits" categories={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed"]}
  series={[{id:"this-week", label:"This week", values:[38, 55, 48]}]}
  domain={[0, 60]} variant="area" />
notes: The chart shows dates and a quiet dot grid by default. Enable showYAxis when numeric levels need to be visible at a glance.
Series names appear in the inspection readout. Set showLegend when the key needs to be visible before interaction.
Supply equally spaced categories in reading order and up to four named series with the same number of values. Null and nonfinite values leave gaps. Zero is an observation.

Use a shared domain containing all observations when comparing separate charts. Area shading belongs to the first series. Line styles distinguish the series independently of color. Set curve to linear for straight segments.
Explore values by hovering, tapping, or using arrow keys, Home and End. The default number format is English; supply formatValue and translated empty, missing and navigation labels for other locales.

name: BarChart
description: Grouped or stacked columns for comparing values across categories on a shared zero baseline.
code:
<BarChart label="Hours by team" categories={["Product", "Design", "Growth"]}
  series={[
    {id:"actual", label:"Actual", values:[38, 29, 46]},
    {id:"plan", label:"Plan", values:[32, 36, 40]}
  ]} />
notes: Use layout stacked for additive series. Positive and negative values accumulate independently on either side of zero. A custom domain must contain the cumulative bounds.

Use layout percent for nonnegative shares on a fixed 0–100% scale. The readout shows each share of the observed total and its raw value. A zero total leaves the column empty and shows raw zeros. Supply formatShare to localize percentages.
Series names appear in the inspection readout. Set showLegend when the key needs to be visible before interaction.
Pass up to four series in display order with one value per category. Put the primary series first to give it the accent fill. Comparison series use outline and dash styling as well as color.

Grouped columns start at zero and reserve empty slots for missing observations. In stacks, zero and missing observations take no space and remain distinguishable in the readout. Use the same domain to compare separate charts.
Explore exact values by hovering, tapping, or using arrow keys, Home and End. Supply formatValue and translated empty, missing and navigation labels for other locales.

name: DonutChart
description: Shares of a whole with an in-ring total and exact values on inspection.
code:
<DonutChart label="Traffic sources" totalLabel="Visits" items={[
  {id:"direct", label:"Direct", value:6420},
  {id:"search", label:"Search", value:3720},
  {id:"referrals", label:"Referrals", value:1960}
]} />
notes: Pass up to six mutually exclusive categories in display order. Values must be finite and nonnegative. The ring uses their sum as the whole.
Hover, tap or use arrow keys, Home and End to inspect a category. Its name, exact value and share appear inside the ring. Enable showLegend when readers need the category names before interacting.
An empty list displays the empty label. All-zero data displays a total of zero and omits percentages. Supply formatValue and formatShare for localized output.

name: CompositionBar
description: One proportional bar with visible category amounts, shares or both.
code:
<CompositionBar label="Storage by file type" items={[
  {id:"originals", label:"Originals", value:54},
  {id:"exports", label:"Exports", value:24},
  {id:"backups", label:"Backups", value:14}
]} readout="both" formatValue={value => `${value} GB`} />
notes: Use in a card or narrow panel to show a few mutually exclusive parts of one whole. Pass up to six finite nonnegative values with stable unique IDs and a meaningful label.
The bar preserves category order and proportional segment widths. Keep that order consistent across views of the same categories. Use BarChart with layout="percent" to compare several totals.

Choose inline readouts for short labels or rows for shared numeric alignment. Use value, share or both depending on what readers need. Exact readouts remain visible without pointer or keyboard interaction.
Zero-valued categories stay in the list without taking bar width. All-zero data shows values and omits shares. An empty list uses emptyLabel.

name: Heatmap
description: A two-axis matrix that shows intensity and reveals exact cell values.
code:
<Heatmap label="Requests by hour" columns={["08:00", "10:00", "12:00"]}
  rows={[
    {id:"mon", label:"Mon", values:[4, 13, 23]},
    {id:"tue", label:"Tue", values:[7, null, 32]}
  ]} max={40} />
notes: Supply a value for each column. Values are finite and nonnegative; null represents a missing observation and gets a dashed tile. Zero is an observed value.
Use the same max across matrices that should be compared. Hover, tap or use arrow keys to inspect exact values in a tooltip beside the cell. Home and End move within a row.
Keep axis labels short at the target width. Provide formatValue and localized labels when needed.

name: ScatterChart
description: Paired numeric observations for inspecting how two measures vary together.
code:
<ScatterChart label="Response time by traffic" xLabel="Requests / sec" yLabel="Response time (ms)" points={[
  {id:"run-1", label:"Run 1", x:12, y:110},
  {id:"run-2", label:"Run 2", x:52, y:162},
  {id:"run-3", label:"Run 3", x:104, y:301}
]} />
notes: Give each point a stable ID and finite x and y values. Label both axes with their units.
Use matching xDomain and yDomain to compare separate plots. Use formatX and formatY for localized values.
Inspect the nearest point with the pointer or traverse observations in supplied order with the keyboard.

name: RangeChart
description: Low and high values by category, with an optional midpoint.
code:
<RangeChart label="Response time (ms)" lowLabel="P10" highLabel="P90" midpointLabel="Median" items={[
  {id:"mon", label:"Mon", low:84, high:162, midpoint:119},
  {id:"tue", label:"Tue", low:92, high:176, midpoint:125}
]} />
notes: Use a shared scale to compare intervals. Supply a midpoint only when it adds information, such as a measured median.
Use null bounds for missing observations and give the bounds meaningful labels with units. Inspect a category to read its exact values.

name: DumbbellChart
description: Paired values on one scale for comparing before and after across groups.
code:
<DumbbellChart label="Response time before and after" items={[
  {id:"api", label:"API", before:242, after:164},
  {id:"billing", label:"Billing", before:153, after:190}
]} formatValue={(value) => `${value} ms`} />
notes: The hollow point marks Before and the filled point marks After. Equal values share a position. A null endpoint leaves the other point visible.
Compare the same measure in the same units. Supply a shared domain when comparing separate charts and use formatValue to include units.
Hover, tap or use the arrow keys to read both values. Rename beforeLabel and afterLabel when comparing other paired conditions.

name: BoxPlot
description: Compare the median, quartiles and spread across groups, such as request latency by service.
code:
<BoxPlot label="Request latency (ms)" items={[
  {id:"api", label:"API", summary:{low:42, q1:74, median:96, q3:128, high:176}, outliers:[203]},
  {id:"search", label:"Search", summary:{low:32, q1:58, median:88, q3:154, high:210}}
]} />
notes: Supply a five-number summary for each group. The box spans Q1 to Q3 and the white line marks the median. Supply whiskers and outliers using the same statistical convention across groups.
Use null for a missing summary. Use the same domain across related charts and include all observations, including outliers.

Hover, tap or focus the plot to inspect the summary and outlier count, even with one group. Use arrow keys to move between groups and Escape to close the readout. Use formatAxisValue for shorter ticks when units are already visible. Set --flood-chart-plot-height on a shared parent to align plot heights with Histogram.

name: BulletChart
description: Actual values and targets on the same horizontal scale.
code:
<BulletChart label="Resolved requests" max={100} items={[
  {id:"web", label:"Web", value:74, target:80},
  {id:"email", label:"Email", value:56, target:50}
]} />
notes: Supply finite nonnegative actuals and targets in the same unit. Use a shared max to compare separate charts.
The fill shows the actual value and the vertical marker shows the target. Both exact values are visible without interaction.

name: Histogram
description: Show how often values such as request latency fall into equal-width intervals.
code: <Histogram label="Request latency distribution" xLabel="Latency (ms)" countLabel="Requests" start={0} binWidth={50} counts={[5, 16, 34, 49, 41, 28, 17, 9, 4, 0]} />
notes: Supply precomputed nonnegative integer counts in ascending bin order. Every bin shares binWidth. Keep interior zero bins so the numeric scale stays continuous.
Count each observation in exactly one interval. A typical convention includes the lower boundary and excludes the upper boundary, with the last upper boundary included if needed.

Compare histograms on the same numeric boundaries and maxCount. Set showXAxisLabel to false when the title already supplies the unit. Hover, tap or use the keyboard to inspect an interval and its exact count.

name: WaterfallChart
description: Signed changes and checkpoints along a running total.
code:
<WaterfallChart label="Net revenue (USD)" steps={[
  {id:"gross", label:"Gross", value:32000, kind:"total"},
  {id:"refunds", label:"Refunds", value:-4500},
  {id:"fees", label:"Fees", value:-2500},
  {id:"net", label:"Net", value:25000, kind:"total"}
]} />
notes: A change adds its signed value to the running total. A total is an absolute checkpoint that replaces the running total.
Use the same domain for charts you want to compare. It must contain zero and every intermediate total. Use formatValue to add units.
Hover, tap or use the keyboard to inspect exact changes and running totals. Decreases use a dashed outline.

name: BarList
description: A compact ranked list of named values on one scale.
code:
<BarList label="Visits by page" items={[
  {id:"overview", label:"Overview", value:214},
  {id:"components", label:"Components", value:136}
]} />
notes: Sort items before passing them in. The list preserves display order and uses a shared zero baseline. Pass the same max to compare separate lists.
Each item uses a proportional background bar from Flood Meter. Labels and exact values share one row and stay aligned across the list. Supply valueText for units or localized formatting.

name: Timeline
description: An ordered display of recorded activity or progress steps with optional descriptions and times.
code: <Timeline label="Ticket activity" mode="activity" items={[{id:"opened",title:"Ticket opened",description:"Maya Chen reported an export issue.",dateTime:"2026-10-26T09:00:00Z",timeLabel:"09:00"},{id:"reproduced",title:"Issue reproduced",description:"Sam Rivera reproduced the failure.",dateTime:"2026-10-26T10:30:00Z",timeLabel:"10:30"}]} />
notes: Use activity mode for chronological records or schedules. Decorative markers retain the shared track, and progress state and stateLabels are ignored.

Use layout=feed for short summaries with inline times and optional rich content, including FileList and CommentThread. Use layout=schedule when comparing times in a shared leading column. Without times, the schedule drops that column. Connector styles mark the span to the next event.
Default progress mode gives each step a visually hidden localized state label. At most one step may be current; use Steps when users navigate between stages.
Supply unique nonempty IDs, nonempty titles and the intended order. timeLabel is user-facing text and dateTime, when supplied, is the machine-readable time. Both are host-owned.
Markers and optional artwork are decorative. Long descriptions and times wrap without changing marker alignment.
Use density=compact for short events in a narrow history panel. Use ActivityTimeline when date groups help people scan longer histories.
Compatible addition in 0.2.5. Uses existing Flood semantic tokens and relative geometry.

name: ActivityTimeline
description: A chronological activity feed with labeled periods and rich event details.
code: <ActivityTimeline label="Export activity" density="compact" groups={[{id:"nov-14",label:"14 November",dateTime:"2026-11-14",items:[{id:"created",title:"Export created",timeLabel:"09:10",dateTime:"2026-11-14T09:10:00Z"}]}]} />
notes: Use separate date groups for a long history. Supply the display label and optional machine-readable date. The host owns time zones, chronological direction and stable IDs.
Each group starts its own event track. Empty groups are omitted. Supply emptyContent when the absence of activity needs an explanation.
Use headingLevel to fit the page outline and density=compact in a constrained panel. Place FileList appearance=embedded or CommentThread in an event's content only when it clarifies that event.

name: NavigationList
description: A grouped list of native navigation links with a clear current destination.
code: <NavigationList label="Project navigation" currentValue="overview" items={[{value:"overview",label:"Overview",href:"/overview",group:"Workspace"},{value:"activity",label:"Activity",href:"/activity",group:"Workspace"},{value:"settings",label:"Settings",href:"/settings",group:"Manage"}]} />
notes: NavigationList renders nav, lists and native anchors; it is not an ARIA menu or tablist. The host supplies unique stable item values, destinations and currentValue. Browser modifier/target navigation is preserved through item.linkProps.

Optional group names label contiguous item groups. Icons are decorative IconSlot content; descriptions remain associated link text. Size controls compact row density while coarse pointer targets remain usable. No routing engine, URL inference or disabled navigation simulation is supplied.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.5 source candidate.

name: Steps
description: An ordered progress sequence with explicit current, completed, upcoming and error states.
code: <Steps label="Project setup" currentValue="access" items={[{value:"details",title:"Details"},{value:"access",title:"Access"},{value:"review",title:"Review"}]} />
notes: Steps renders an ordered list, not tabs. currentValue identifies aria-current=step; preceding steps default to complete and later steps to upcoming. Item status may explicitly mark complete/upcoming/error. Omitted currentValue starts at the first step.

Without onStepChange, steps are informative content. Providing it renders native step buttons; the host owns navigation and currentValue updates. Disabled items only affect those actions. Every state has text through customizable statusLabels; color and icons are additional cues. Horizontal steps reflow based on their available width.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.5 source candidate.

name: StepProgress
description: A compact summary of the current stage in a multi-step form.
code: <StepProgress title="Team access" step={2} totalSteps={3} />
notes: Use in a narrow flow that only needs the current step title and position. Use Steps when people need to see or revisit other stages.

Supply a 1-based step and a positive integer totalSteps. Use formatPosition to localize the visible count. The decorative track shows position in the sequence. The host owns validation and progression.

name: AppShell
description: A workspace layout with optional navigation, top bar and footer, plus a keyboard skip target.
code: <AppShell topBar={<AppTopBar start={<Text>Workspace</Text>} />}><PageHeader title="Projects" /></AppShell>
notes: Use content scrolling for a full-window application, including record queues whose row count changes. It keeps the navigation, top bar and footer outside the work scrollport. Use scroll="page" for a document that scrolls as a whole.
Content mode uses Flood ScrollArea. Set scrollContentInset="none" when existing workspace padding clears the overlay rails and the content width needs to stay fixed.
Supply Sidebar for docked navigation. Set navigationDrawer with a shell-width threshold and Drawer content to swap automatically. Share accepted route and branch state between the two presentations.
Use mainAs="section" only when embedding a shell inside an existing main landmark.

name: AppTopBar
description: Application context and global actions in two independent, wrapping slots.
code: <AppTopBar start={<Text>Workspace</Text>} end={<Button size="sm">Search</Button>} />
notes: Use in AppShell or in a host-owned layout. Use PageHeader for the current page's title and actions.
The start and end groups wrap on narrow hosts without changing keyboard order. Use bordered only where the toolbar needs a visible boundary.

name: PageHeader
description: The main page heading with optional supporting text and page actions.
code: <PageHeader title="Projects" actions={<Button>New project</Button>} />
notes: Use inside main for the page's h1. An embedded preview can choose headingLevel={2}. Use Section for titled content within the page.
Add a description only when it supplies context the title cannot. Keep filters in the collection toolbar.
Actions wrap below the title when the header's own container narrows. The heading stays first in reading and keyboard order.

name: Section
description: A named document section with a compact heading, supporting description and optional actions.
code:
<Section title="Project settings" description="Manage details your team shares." headingLevel={2}>
  <Text as="p">Section content.</Text>
</Section>
notes: Use Section for a named content or settings group. Keep peer sections on the same heading scale and body inset, and set the spacing between groups in their parent. Use Fieldset when related controls need an accessible group legend.
Add a description when it tells the user a condition, consequence or other detail they need. At a narrow width, verify that actions wrap without shrinking the title into unreadable fragments.
Section renders a native section and heading. A generated heading ID labels the region; explicit id creates a deterministic heading ID. headingLevel follows the host document hierarchy.

The title and description share a close text column; actions align separately and wrap when necessary. It adds no surface or border. Compose Surface or another container inside when content needs its own background.
headingLevel chooses h2–h6 for the document outline; it does not set the visual scale. headingSize independently selects the existing Heading typography role (section by default).

name: Split
description: A responsive main-and-supporting layout with logical pane placement and container-based collapse.
code: <Split side="end" ratio="main" collapseAt="md" main={<Text as="p">Main content</Text>} aside={<Text as="p">Supporting content</Text>} />
notes: main and aside are content slots in generic div panes; they do not introduce duplicate main landmarks. side places the supporting pane at logical start/end and preserves the same DOM reading order. ratio chooses equal panes or a 2:1 emphasis on main/aside.

Container queries collapse at sm=30rem, md=48rem or lg=64rem; never retains two columns. gap uses the spacing scale. This is layout composition, with no resizing gesture, saved pane sizes or splitter keyboard model.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.5 source candidate.

name: Center
description: Center a constrained piece of content in both axes of an available region.
code:
<Center minHeight="12rem" maxWidth="24rem">
  <Text as="p">A focused message.</Text>
</Center>
notes: Center supplies two-axis alignment with an inner content wrapper. minHeight sets the available vertical region; maxWidth constrains the content rather than the entire parent. Values are ordinary CSS lengths, preferably rem.

inline opts into inline-grid for centering within text or an inline composition. It adds no content semantics, surface, spacing between siblings or viewport positioning. Use Stack/Inline for collections and Container for page gutters.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.5 source candidate.

name: SkipLink
description: A native skip-navigation link revealed on focus and aimed at a page content target.
code:
<SkipLink href="#main-content" />
<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1}>Page content</main>
notes: Place SkipLink early in DOM order and point href at a nonempty same-page fragment. The target should have tabIndex=-1 (or already be focusable). Native fragment navigation updates the URL; the component then focuses and reveals the target.

It stays visually hidden until focused. The click handler respects prevented events, modifier navigation and new-window targets. Reduced motion uses immediate scrolling. It does not create a focus trap or change the target tabindex.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.5 source candidate.

name: ListBox
description: A named single or multiple selection list with native validation and semantic feedback.
code: <ListBox label="Framework" name="framework" defaultValue="react" options={[{value:"react",label:"React"},{value:"vue",label:"Vue"},{value:"svelte",label:"Svelte"}]} />
notes: Use a scalar value/defaultValue in single mode and an array in multiple mode. onValueChange returns the matching shape. Stable, unique nonempty option IDs are submitted as repeated hidden native form fields when name is supplied. Uncontrolled reset restores the initial selection.

The list owns one Tab stop and aria-activedescendant. Arrows/Home/End move through enabled options; single selection follows navigation. Space/Enter selects or toggles. Typing searches option-label prefixes. Disabled options cannot be selected; readOnly retains navigation and copying without changing the value.

Provide a clear label or use hideLabel with the accessible label preserved. Use disabled on the composite to remove its Tab stop. The list is not virtualized and does not fetch options. Available in 0.2.5.
required validates accepted selection; readonly bypasses validation and disabled excludes form values.
Use option avatar for people. Mixed rows reserve a shared avatar slot so names and descriptions start on the same axis.
The surface appearance uses Flood ScrollArea for bounded lists. Use plain when a parent surface already owns scrolling.
description/message and status share the field feedback contract. validationMessage is a host-owned blocking constraint.

name: PinInput
description: One native code editor presented as a compact row of character slots.
code: <PinInput label="Verification code" name="code" length={6} autoComplete="one-time-code" required />
notes: One real native input preserves mobile one-time-code autofill, clipboard, selection, forms and required validity; decorative slots are hidden from assistive technology. Use its native ref for focus. The host owns verification and authentication.

length is an integer from 1 to 12. mode numeric permits ASCII digits; alphanumeric also permits ASCII letters. Paste strips separators and invalid characters, then respects the selection and length. Backspace and arrow editing remain native. Use mask to visually conceal the code.

Use value/onValueChange or defaultValue. Native form reset restores the initial uncontrolled value. Pattern validity requires a complete code when nonempty; required also rejects an empty code. Translate label and preserve its accessible name with hideLabel. Available in 0.2.5.

name: RatingValue
description: A fractional star rating or compact score for cards, lists and tables.
code: <RatingValue value={4.7} count={128} />
notes: Use RatingValue for an observed score. Use Rating when people can enter their own rating.
Use stars in spacious cards and compact for dense rows where one star and the numeric scale fit. The optional count is announced together with the score.

Pass null when no rating exists and use unratedLabel to localize the empty state. Zero is a valid rating. lang formats the visible numbers, and a localized aria-label can describe the score, scale and count.

name: RatingSummary
description: An aggregate star rating and distribution across scores.
code: <RatingSummary label="Customer ratings" counts={[2, 0, 4, 20, 102]} />
notes: Pass counts for one star through the highest score, in ascending order. A zero preserves the bucket. The weighted average, total and bars derive from those same counts.

Use for an aggregate in a review panel or drawer. The default auto layout places the overview beside the bars where it fits and stacks them in a narrow column. Use stacked when the host needs one column.
The distribution reads highest to lowest, with each bar measured against all ratings. All-zero counts show the localized empty state.
Set lang to format numbers. Use labels to localize the empty text, count, spoken score and bucket names. Use RatingValue for a score alone and Rating to collect feedback.

name: Rating
description: A compact star rating backed by a named native radio group.
code: <Rating label="Your experience" name="experience" defaultValue={3} max={5} />
notes: Provide a nonempty name for native radio grouping and form submission. value/defaultValue are integers from zero (unselected) to max; max is an integer from 1 to 10. Uncontrolled native reset restores defaultValue. required uses native group validation.

Arrow keys follow logical direction, Home/End jump to the first/last value, and Space selects the focused radio. One radio is in Tab order. readOnly keeps the current selection focusable without allowing changes; disabled is native.

Use getValueLabel to localize each radio name. The stars are decorative; native named radios carry the value. hideLabel preserves the legend for assistive technology. No fractional values or review submission engine is included. Available in 0.2.5.

name: Dropzone
description: A file drop target composed with the native Flood FileInput.
code: <Dropzone label="Project attachments" name="attachments" multiple accept=".pdf,image/*" />
notes: The existing FileInput remains the real chooser and successful native form control. Dropping files dispatches the same selection flow: multiple appends and deduplicates; single selection keeps the first dropped file. Native form reset and per-file removal remain intact.

The zone responds only to file drags and prevents navigation on file drop. Disabled fields reject drops. Translate label/description and FileInput action labels. The chooser remains keyboard accessible; dropping is an additional pointer workflow.
Use compact density when the field shares a drawer or a small form. Use FileDropTarget when the files belong to an application-owned queue.
accept guides the native chooser; validate file types, size and contents in the host. No file contents are read. Available in 0.2.5.

name: FileDropTarget
description: A keyboard-accessible file picker and drop target for an upload or import queue.
code: <FileDropTarget label="Import files" accept=".csv" onFilesSelect={addToQueue} />
notes: Choose when the application owns the upload or import queue. Both drop and native pick call onFilesSelect with the newly chosen files. The same file can be chosen again.
Set multiple=false for a single file. Disabled targets prevent browser navigation on drop and ignore the files. Localize chooseLabel, label and description.
Use UploadList for actual transfer status and Dropzone when files belong in native FormData. The host owns validation, ordering, duplicate policy and upload.
accept guides the native chooser and does not validate dropped files.

name: CharacterCount
description: Supporting character or remaining-length feedback with an explicit over-limit message.
code: <CharacterCount value="Make room for a clear idea." max={80} htmlFor="project-note" />
notes: Pass text through value or supply an explicit nonnegative integer count for a host-defined counting rule. The default text count uses Unicode code points, not UTF-16 code units or grapheme clusters. max is advisory and does not truncate or validate an editor.

mode remaining displays max minus count; count displays the current count and optional limit. An over-limit message is visible in addition to its semantic color. Translate label/overLimitLabel; lang formats the number.

Use htmlFor to associate supporting output with its editor and aria-describedby on the editor when appropriate. Live announcements default off to avoid announcing every keystroke; the host may opt into aria-live. Available in 0.2.5.

name: Editable
description: Inline editing with explicit save/cancel and a committed form value.
code: <Editable label="Project name" defaultValue="Flood workspace" name="project" />
notes: Preview and edit modes keep a separate draft. Enter commits and Escape cancels; IME composition does not submit.
Use blurAction to commit, cancel or preserve the draft on outside focus. Moving focus to the save/cancel actions is internal to the editor.
The host owns controlled value and editing props; callbacks request changes. The hidden named form field contains only the committed value.
readOnly keeps a copyable field; disabled prevents editing. Localized action labels and inputRef are available. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: TagInput
description: Free-form text tokens with keyboard entry, removal and named form values.
code: <TagInput label="Topics" defaultValue={["Design", "React"]} name="topics" placeholder="Add a topic…" />
notes: Use TagInput for values the user may create. Use MultiSelect for a fixed option collection.
Enter and configured delimiters commit trimmed, unique tags. Pasting separated text adds multiple tags. IME composition is preserved.
Each committed tag submits one entry under name. required applies to committed tags; a draft is not a submitted token. Form reset preserves controlled ownership.
Use maxVisibleTags to keep a dense field compact. The count reveals the hidden tags for inspection or removal, and the form always submits all committed values.
Backspace on an empty draft removes the last visible token. Read only preserves inspection and form values; disabled omits submission and removal. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: CommandList
description: Search and invoke commands with grouped results and keyboard navigation.
code: <CommandList label="Search commands" items={[{id:"new",label:"New project",group:"Projects"},{id:"settings",label:"Open settings",group:"Workspace"}]} onAction={id => console.log(id)} />
notes: CommandList invokes actions; Combobox and MultiSelect edit form values. A command list has no submitted name or persistent selected value.
Typing filters labels, descriptions, group names and keywords. Arrow keys, Home/End and Enter navigate and invoke enabled commands. Escape remains available to a host Dialog.
Use icon for a decorative command glyph and shortcut for a display hint describing a host-registered binding. Mixed rows share their label axis as results are filtered.
Use query/onQueryChange for host ownership or defaultQuery for local filtering. Loading blocks stale invocation and exposes an announcement; the host owns asynchronous work and cancellation.

The ref targets the native search input. Native div props target the wrapper. Translate labels, placeholder, emptyMessage and loadingMessage; hideLabel preserves the search name. No modal, global shortcut or router integration is implied. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: NotificationTrigger
description: An inbox button with a quiet unread marker and an accessible exact count.
code: <Popover title="Notifications" chrome="title-only" style={{padding:"var(--flood-sys-space-3)"}} trigger={props => <NotificationTrigger {...props} label="Notifications" unreadCount={1} />}><NotificationInbox appearance="overlay" label="Recent notifications" items={[{id:"mention",title:"Maya mentioned you",href:"/reviews/48",unread:true}]} /></Popover>
notes: Place NotificationTrigger among global header actions. Compose it with an overlay trigger or a host-owned onClick. The overlay owns expanded state and focus restoration.
Supply the host's accepted unread count. A dot appears only above zero and takes no layout space. Use formatUnread to localize the exact count added to the button's name.
Use NotificationInbox appearance=overlay inside the floating surface for tighter rows and an unread marker beside the title.
Use a link to navigate to a full-page inbox. Use a separate CountBadge beside a visible label when people need to compare exact counts while scanning.

name: SearchTrigger
description: A button for opening search, with a compact icon-only option and an optional keyboard hint.
code: <CommandPalette title="Find a page" searchLabel="Search pages" items={[{id:"projects",label:"Projects"}]} onAction={id => {}} trigger={props => <SearchTrigger {...props} label="Find a page" />} />
notes: Use SearchTrigger to open search in another surface. Use SearchInput when people can enter a query in place.
Use iconOnly in a compact toolbar and fullWidth in a wider sidebar. Keep the label meaningful in either layout.
Supply shortcut and aria-keyshortcuts only when the host has implemented that binding. The keycap is hidden for coarse pointers and icon-only triggers.

name: CommandPalette
description: A modal search surface for navigating pages or running commands.
code: <CommandPalette title="Go to page" searchLabel="Search pages" trigger={props => <Button {...props}>Go to page</Button>} items={[{id:"projects",label:"All projects"}]} onAction={id => console.log(id)} />
notes: Choose comfortable or compact density. Items can be grouped, described or disabled and share CommandList's optional icons and shortcut hints.
Opening focuses search. Enter or click runs an enabled action and requests closure. Escape and the close button return focus to the trigger.
Use controlled query and loading for asynchronous search. The application owns requests, navigation and any global shortcut.

name: DateField
description: Segmented Gregorian date entry with canonical form values and explicit date validation.
code: <DateField label="Start date" name="start" defaultValue="2026-10-26" order="day-month-year" />
notes: Uses three native text segments rather than an operating-system calendar popup. Calendar and DatePicker are separate contracts.
Values are canonical YYYY-MM-DD dates from 0001 through 9999, or an empty string. min/max and leap years use civil date arithmetic without timezones.
Arrow keys adjust segments. Left/Right move at segment boundaries; IME and modifier shortcuts remain available. Use explicit order and localized segmentLabels/messages.
In editable fields, incomplete or invalid drafts block native submission; the hidden named field contains no stale previous date. Controlled values and form resets preserve host ownership.

Read only retains copying and accepted canonical submission, even outside current bounds or application constraints. It bypasses native validity without accepting partial or refused drafts. Disabled fields and fieldsets remain excluded. Introduced in the unpublished 0.2.7 source candidate.

name: TimeField
description: Segmented 24-hour time entry with canonical values, bounds and a seconds-based step.
code: <TimeField label="Start time" name="startTime" defaultValue="09:30" step={300} />
notes: Use HH:mm with minute precision or HH:mm:ss with second precision. Values have no date or timezone.
step is expressed in seconds and anchored to min or midnight; minute precision requires a multiple of 60. Overnight ranges are not inferred.

In editable fields, incomplete, invalid, out-of-range, step-mismatched and refused controlled drafts block native submission. Readonly preserves accepted canonical time outside bounds/step alignment; it never accepts a partial or refused draft. Disabled values are excluded.
Click the control background to focus a missing or remembered segment. Keyboard steps, Home/End, paste and IME preserve host cancellation. Translate segmentLabels and messages. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: Calendar
description: One calendar with day, month and year views, without nested popups.
code: <Calendar label="Choose a date" defaultValue="2026-10-26" today="2026-10-26" weekStartsOn={1} />
notes: Calendar is a standalone visual collection. DateField handles text entry and DatePicker composes the field and calendar layer.
Values use canonical YYYY-MM-DD and visibleMonth uses YYYY-MM. Locale formats Gregorian month/day names; weekStartsOn is explicit.
Arrows move dates; Home/End move within a week and PageUp/PageDown navigate months. Controlled month refusal preserves a real focused day. Disabled dates remain discoverable but cannot select.

The host owns selected values, availability and side effects. Provide today for a deterministic clock in tests or rendering. Min/max bound navigation; readonly prevents selection while allowing browsing. Introduced in 0.2.7.
Month and year controls replace the content of this calendar. Selecting a navigation period returns to days without changing the selected date.
granularity="day" | "month" | "year" chooses YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY.

name: DatePicker
description: A segmented date field with an integrated calendar picker and shared form value.
code: <DatePicker label="Start date" name="start" defaultValue="2026-10-26" today="2026-10-26" />
notes: Composes Flood DateField, Calendar and Popover; text input and visual selection share one canonical value and form bridge.
Activate the calendar icon or Alt+ArrowDown in a segment. Escape/outside dismissal returns or preserves intended focus through the existing overlay engine. Selecting a day closes the calendar.
Read only and disabled prevent opening or date changes; native disabled fieldsets remain inert. Invalid/incomplete drafts retain native DateField validation.

Controlled value and open state are independently host-owned. Native form reset restores the initial uncontrolled date and preserves cancelled resets. Translate calendarLabel/openCalendarLabel, month navigation, segment labels and messages.
DateField remains the keyboard-entry primitive; Calendar remains independently usable. Introduced in the unpublished 0.2.7 source candidate.

name: ErrorSummary
description: A linked validation summary that focuses host-owned invalid fields.
code: <ErrorSummary title="Review the form" errors={[{id:"project",fieldId:"project",message:"Enter a project name."}]} />
notes: The host supplies validation messages. Keep each field error visible next to its field and link to its exact control ID from errors. Use formErrors for messages with no individual correction target.
Use appearance=inline inside a panel when the form already has a surface. The compact appearance preserves the same links and announcement behavior.
Normal activation focuses the target while modifier navigation remains native. onSelect can cancel the action before focus moves.

announcement defaults to off. autoFocus brings a newly shown summary into view and suppresses duplicate live announcements. Updating messages in an existing summary leaves focus where it is. With no field or form errors, the summary renders nothing. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: ResizablePanels
description: Two panels separated by an accessible pointer and keyboard resize control.
code: <ResizablePanels label="Resize workspace" main={<Text>Navigation</Text>} secondary={<Text>Workspace</Text>} style={{height:"16rem"}} />
notes: Percentages describe the main pane and exclude the dedicated separator track. The host supplies content and scrolling.
Drag the separator or use logical arrow keys, Home/End and Shift for large steps. Horizontal resizing follows RTL direction.
value/onValueChange keeps the host in control. onValueCommit reports an accepted completed interaction; pointer cancellation restores the initial uncontrolled size.
The separator occupies space so its touch area does not overlap panel content. Persisting layout and larger panel graphs belong to the host. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: RangeCalendar
description: A Gregorian grid for selecting and previewing one continuous date interval.
code: <RangeCalendar label="Choose travel dates" today="2026-10-26" defaultValue={{start:"2026-10-12",end:"2026-10-18"}} />
notes: The first activation chooses a start; the second completes a normalized ordered interval. Hover and focus can preview an unfinished interval without committing.
Controlled values include partial {start,end:""}; the host must accept that partial value to advance selection. onRangeSelect confirms an enabled completed interval.
isDateDisabled controls endpoints. isRangeDisabled validates the entire interval; interior blocked dates are not inferred by scanning arbitrary date spans.
Reuses the Calendar grid, month navigation, focus and localization contracts. Translate rangeLabels for instruction messages. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: DateRangeField
description: Two segmented date fields with one ordered range and atomic form values.
code: <DateRangeField label="Travel dates" startName="start" endName="end" defaultValue={{start:"2026-10-12",end:"2026-10-18"}} />
notes: The value is {start,end}, with canonical YYYY-MM-DD dates or empty endpoints. Editable partial, reversed, unavailable and refused ranges block native submission. Readonly submits a complete ordered accepted pair despite current bounds/availability; partial, reversed and refused pairs stay atomic empty values.
Both named bridges represent one range contract. The group owns relationship validation while each DateField preserves its calendar validity and keyboard behavior.
Start/end names and labels are explicit; min/max, readonly/disabled, status and form reset follow the field contracts.
Use DateRangePicker for visual interval selection. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: DateRangePicker
description: Paired date entry with one calendar popup for continuous interval selection.
code: <DateRangePicker label="Travel dates" startName="start" endName="end" today="2026-10-26" defaultValue={{start:"2026-10-12",end:"2026-10-18"}} />
notes: Composes DateRangeField, RangeCalendar and the existing Popover engine. One popup selects start and end; it closes after an enabled complete interval.
The popup follows the whole fields region width and clamps to the viewport. Text and calendar editing share the same partial/complete range contract.
Controlled range/open state and availability remain host-owned. Escape/outside dismissal does not turn an incomplete range into a valid submission.
Translate endpoint, calendar and range instruction labels. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: ContextMenu
description: Context actions at the pointer or keyboard target, sharing the Menu interaction engine.
code: <ContextMenu label="Project actions" items={[{id:"rename",label:"Rename"},{id:"duplicate",label:"Duplicate"}]} onAction={id => console.log(id)}><Surface padding="6">Right-click or use Shift+F10.</Surface></ContextMenu>
notes: Right click opens at the pointer; ContextMenu or Shift+F10 opens near the actual focused target. The wrapper is keyboard-focusable and named.
Uses the same Menu items, preferences, nested layers, typeahead and keyboard navigation. Leaf commands close the tree; Escape unwinds one level and restores the real source focus.
disabled preserves the native browser context menu. Controlled open and onAction remain host-owned. Provide a visible Menu action as a primary alternative on touch devices. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: Tree
description: A selectable application hierarchy with independent expansion and keyboard focus.
code: <Tree label="Project files" items={[{value:"source",label:"Source",children:[{value:"button",label:"Button.tsx"}]}]} />
notes: Tree uses tree/treeitem/group semantics, logical arrows, Home/End and typeahead. Moving focus does not select an item. Enter/Space explicitly selects; multiple selection does not cascade.

Items have globally unique values. Expansion uses expandedValues/defaultExpandedValues/onExpandedValuesChange; selection uses value/defaultValue/onValueChange. Controlled refusal preserves the host state.

Read-only allows browsing without selecting. Disabled items remain discoverable but cannot select or expand. hasChildren/loading represent host-owned deferred branches; no fetching or virtualization is built in.
Application selection writes no form values. Use NavigationTree for ordinary native links. Introduced in 0.2.7.

name: NavigationItem
description: One shared navigation row for destinations, commands and independent disclosure.
code: <NavigationItem label="Projects" href="/projects" current />
notes: Uses Flood Link or Button; navigation links remain native anchors with host handlers. Commands and destination clicks do not silently toggle a branch.

disclosure without a destination makes the complete row a disclosure button. href plus disclosure creates separate link and disclosure targets in one shared surface; expanded is controlled by the host.
compact leaf rows retain names through Tooltip. Use NavigationTree for compact branches and link-plus-branch items so the full navigation remains reachable in a Popover.
Pass compactBadge with count and a localized label to show a passive unread dot on the compact control. Supply an expanded count through trailing where useful.

Set labelOverflow=truncate for dense rows with recognizable prefixes. The full label opens from the existing link or button only when clipped. The disclosure and sibling actions keep their own targets.
IconSlot owns leading artwork; IconButton keeps the disclosure target with smaller supporting artwork. trailing is noninteractive metadata, not a place to nest another button inside a link.
trailingAction is an independent sibling control in expanded rows. It is visible alongside any trailing metadata. Use a named IconButton and apply its own disabled state.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.11 source candidate.

name: NavigationGroup
description: Related navigation with optional headings, section actions, separators and disclosure.
code:
<NavigationGroup label="Projects">
  <NavigationItem label="Design system" href="/projects/design" />
  <NavigationItem label="Website" href="/projects/website" />
</NavigationGroup>
notes: Groups related navigation without inventing routes or application-menu semantics. Compose actual NavigationItem destinations or NavigationTree children.
label, hideLabel, headingAction and separator are independent optional presentation choices. Keep headings and separators only when they clarify real relationships.
collapsible uses Flood Collapsible and independent expanded/defaultExpanded/onExpandedChange state; an unaccepted request does not hide accepted content.
Compact mode keeps destinations reachable while removing redundant heading text; compare section actions and body rows on the same rail axis.
Original compatible addition in the unpublished 0.2.11 source candidate.

name: NavigationTree
description: Nested native navigation links with separate disclosure controls.
code: <NavigationTree label="Documentation" defaultExpandedValues={["start"]} items={[{value:"start",label:"Getting started",children:[{value:"installation",label:"Installation",href:"/docs/installation"}]}]} />
notes: Native nav, lists and anchors preserve ordinary Tab order and browser modifier navigation. This component does not use ARIA tree/menu/tab roles.

A branch may have both href and children: its native link navigates while a separate disclosure button expands. currentValue marks the matching destination; ancestors are expanded explicitly by the host.

Expansion is controlled or uncontrolled through expandedValues/defaultExpandedValues/onExpandedValuesChange. Translate disclosure names with expandLabel; content can render host-owned loading or empty branch content.
Item values must be globally unique and children acyclic. Disabled destinations have no active href; parent disability does not propagate to children. Introduced in 0.2.7.

compact creates an icon rail with real leaf links and full Popover navigation for branches. flyoutSide controls placement; current descendant styling is separate from aria-current. trailing accepts metadata in expanded rows. Compact labels remain accessible and have native title hints.
currentKind defaults to page. Use location when the active value identifies a broader global navigation context rather than the exact current page.
Enable branchGuides for dense nested lists. Item trailingAction uses the shared NavigationItem slot in expanded rows and on destinations inside branch flyouts.
labelOverflow is forwarded to destination and disclosure rows, including the expanded navigation inside branch flyouts.

name: ColorSwatch
description: A named sample of an opaque RGB color.
code: <ColorSwatch label="Flood pink" value="#ff47a8" />
notes: Opaque RGB colors only; keep a text label wherever color conveys meaning.

name: ColorPalette
description: A compact set of named color choices for one application-owned value.
code: <ColorPalette label="Accent colors" options={[{value: "#ff47a8", label: "Pink"}, {value: "#78b8ff", label: "Blue"}]} value={accent} onValueChange={setAccent} />
notes: Use a palette when the available colors are predetermined. Use labeled appearance when names distinguish colors or clarify their purpose. Every swatch has a name even in the compact appearance.
The host owns the accepted color. The active option has a perimeter and a pressed state. A color outside the options leaves the group without a pressed choice.
Inputs are opaque hex colors; callbacks receive normalized six-digit hex. Use ColorPicker for typed or RGB edits and native form submission.

name: ColorPicker
description: An RGB color editor with hex input, channel sliders and reusable presets.
code: <ColorPicker label="Accent color" defaultValue="#ff47a8" name="accent" presets={["#ff47a8", "#ffffff", "#78b8ff"]} />
notes: Uses #rrggbb values without alpha or gradients.
The hex field owns native form validation; RGB controls provide an additional editing path.

name: HoverCard
description: A focusable preview that opens on hover, keyboard focus or explicit activation.
code:
<HoverCard title="Alex Morgan" trigger={props => <Button {...props} variant="subtle">Alex Morgan</Button>}>
  <Text as="p" size="compact">Designer at Flood.</Text>
  <Link href="https://github.com/tillwithered">View profile</Link>
</HoverCard>
notes: Interactive content belongs to a named dialog preview, not a tooltip.
Click pins the preview; keyboard and touch users can activate the trigger.

name: TreeSelect
description: Single selection from a hierarchical collection inside a popup.
code: <TreeSelect label="Destination" name="destination" items={[{value:"design",label:"Design",selectable:false,children:[{value:"foundations",label:"Foundations"},{value:"components",label:"Components"}]}]} />
notes: This first version selects one item; Tree provides standalone multiple selection.
Values are globally unique and expansion remains independent of selection.

name: DateTimePicker
description: A composed civil date and wall-clock time with separate form values.
code: <DateTimePicker label="Schedule" dateName="date" timeName="time" defaultValue={{date:"2026-10-26",time:"09:30"}} />
notes: Date and time submit as separate fields. No timezone, UTC conversion or instant is inferred.
Date bounds and daily time bounds are independent. Use application validation for cross-field business rules.

name: DataList
description: A native list of structured rows with independent links and actions.
code:
<DataList>
  <DataListItem title="Design system" description="Foundations and components" metadata="Updated today" />
  <DataListItem title="Website" description="Documentation and examples" metadata="Updated yesterday" />
</DataList>
notes: For authored items, keep the visible author and message together. Keep a row action associated with its record and test long content beside the action. Choose Timeline if sequence is the organizing idea.
This is a ul/li list, not a listbox or data grid.
A selectable DataListItem reserves a leading checkbox track across its peers. Set reserveSelectionSpace when filtering may temporarily hide them all.
Keep navigation in the title link and actions in their own buttons.

name: DataListItem
description: A structured list row with media, supporting text, metadata and actions.
code:
<DataList>
  <DataListItem title="Design system" description="Foundations and components" metadata="Updated today" />
</DataList>
notes: Render inside DataList or another native list.
The row is not clickable; supply a Link as title when navigation is needed.
Pass selection with label, checked, onCheckedChange and optional disabled for host-owned bulk selection. The checkbox is independent from the title link and row actions.
Place a MetadataList in details for facts that belong with the title. Keep values compared across siblings in trailing metadata.
In a narrow DataList, default rows with both metadata and actions move that pair beneath the copy, keeping the actions on the trailing edge.

Use layout=content for comments and feedback with a multiline body. Place the Avatar in media, author in title, and message in description. DataList moves trailing metadata and actions beneath the copy when the list container is narrow.

name: NotificationItem
description: A persistent inbox row with independent navigation and read controls.
code: <NotificationList label="Inbox"><NotificationItem title="Maya mentioned you" href="/reviews/48" unread timeLabel="09:24" /></NotificationList>
notes: Use for persistent updates that people need to revisit. Supply a concise title, optional secondary context and a host-formatted time.
In a narrow NotificationList, time and actions move below the copy. The timestamp starts on the title edge and the action stays at the trailing edge.
At wider widths, time and the read action share the trailing row.
The title is a native link when href is present. The independent read control appears with onUnreadChange. Host code owns unread state and may update it when the user opens a destination.
Unread status is also exposed as text for assistive technology. Translate unreadLabel, markReadLabel and markUnreadLabel when needed.

name: NotificationInbox
description: A persistent inbox with an unread filter and independent read actions.
code: <NotificationInbox label="Project notifications" items={[{id:"mention",title:"Maya mentioned you",href:"/reviews/48",unread:true,timeLabel:"09:24"}]} />
notes: Use for updates people can revisit. The All and Unread controls filter the supplied items. Use filter and onFilterChange when the host needs to control the choice.
Read actions request changes via onUnreadChange or onMarkAllRead. The host accepts changes through items. Use markingAllRead while the bulk request runs.

Use state=loading for the initial load. Match loadingPlaceholder to the row content. Use state=error with onRetry and retrying for a failed load. Keep state=ready during a refresh if previously loaded updates remain usable.
The list distinguishes an empty inbox from an inbox whose updates have been read. Focus returns to the active filter if a focused row leaves the list.

name: NotificationList
description: A named list of persistent notifications with shared media, copy and action tracks.
code: <NotificationList label="Inbox"><NotificationItem title="Export ready for review" unread timeLabel="09:24" /><NotificationItem title="Settings updated" timeLabel="Yesterday" /></NotificationList>
notes: Use stable host IDs as keys and a visible or accessible list name. Use a shared density for peer rows. Start with spacing alone and enable dividers if dense rows are hard to distinguish.
Read and unread rows retain their geometry when mixed, and rows share a text axis even when some omit media. Provide media only when it identifies a person or event.
Use ToastRegion for transient action feedback and Timeline for chronological history. The inbox holds items a person can revisit.

name: CheckCard
description: A native checkbox presented as a selectable content card.
code: <CheckCard label="Product updates" description="A monthly summary of new features." name="updates" value="product" />
notes: Uses native checkbox semantics, including mixed state, required and form reset.
Use indicatorPlacement=end when the label or an icon should lead the card. Keep placement consistent inside a group.
In a narrow card, metadata moves beneath the main copy so labels and descriptions have more room.
Content is noninteractive: do not nest links or actions inside a card label.

name: CheckCardGroup
description: A responsive group of independently selectable cards.
code: <CheckCardGroup legend="Email subscriptions" name="subscriptions" defaultValue={["security"]} options={[{value:"product",label:"Product updates",metadata:"Monthly"},{value:"security",label:"Security advisories",metadata:"As needed"}]} />
notes: Use when selecting several options with details that inform the choice. The host can control the selected values. Native forms submit one value per checked enabled option with the shared name.

Set minItemWidth for the longest localized card content. The group wraps based on its own width, keeps input order, and inherits Fieldset feedback and disabling. Use indicatorPlacement to place every checkbox at the same logical edge.

name: RadioCardGroup
description: A responsive set of cards for choosing exactly one option.
